text:
talia: heads-up — bringing up balboa21b-int4 on canary GPUs tonight. seeing fragmentation spikes and a couple of CUDA OOMs under bursty traffic. starting thread to coordinate tuning + quickbench.
sam: copy. which infra flavor? 48GB A100 or 80GB?
talia: 48GB A100 pool (dedicated). workload is multi-turn chat with lots of short prompts + occasional long completion (~300-800 tokens).
kj: common pattern — prefix KV cache ballooning with many short sessions. did you enable slot compact/soft-reserve?
talia: soft-reserve on, compacting enabled, but eviction latency looks high. throwing logs below.
```
[2024-11-09T02:34:12Z] token_gen: alloc_kv_cache size=1.2GB
[2024-11-09T02:34:12Z] kernel: prefetched 4 segments (window=2)
[2024-11-09T02:34:12Z] evict: scheduled in 1200ms
[2024-11-09T02:34:13Z] CUDA OOM at kv_cache_alloc (requested 256MB)
stack: kernel::alloc_kv -> kv_manager::ensure_capacity -> cuda::malloc
```
sam: hmm alloc_kv right after prefetch — suggests prefetch window too aggressive for this mix.
kj: what are current defaults? prefetch_window=2, max_batch_tokens=4096, default_max_new_tokens=512.
talia: yep those are the defaults. also seeing p99 latency spikes when eviction kicks in.
perf-bot: benchmark summary (canary snapshot 1765432199-run1): p50=68ms, p95=210ms, p99=480ms, token_cost=0.012 tkns/usd, kernel_evictions=1.8/min, mem_frag_index=0.27
sam: kernel_evictions >1/min on 48GB is high. quick mitigations:
- reduce prefetch_window to 1
- lower default_max_new_tokens to 256 for balboa21b-int4
- enable microbatching with smaller batch size and faster batch timeout
- tune eviction_threshold_ms down from 1200 -> 600
kj: agree. microbatch snippet I tested earlier:
```
serving.config:
  batch_timeout_ms: 3
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  prefetch_window: 1
  eviction_threshold_ms: 600
  soft_reserve_mb: 1024
```
sam: also try gentle slowstart: limit concurrency to 0.7 of host capacity during first 6h of rollout.
talia: will run a quick A/B: baseline vs. tuned settings above. also want to check quality change after lowering max_new_tokens — will run evals on our convo set.
kj: note: lowering max_new_tokens reduces worst-case allocation, but you might still OOM on single very long requests. consider server-side enforced max_request_tokens=1024 and client-side hinting.
perf-bot: quick eval snapshot (prequant vs int4 tuned): exact-match QA delta -0.6%, rouge delta -0.4%, latency change +3% (with tuned microbatching), mem_frag_index -> 0.12, kernel_evictions -> 0.3/min
talia: those quality deltas look acceptable for most customers. thanks perf-bot.
sam: rollout plan proposal:
- canary 5% with tuned serving.config for 2h
- if kernel_evictions < 0.5/min and p99 < 600ms, expand to 25% for 6h
- enable slowstart soft cap for first 24h
- schedule a regression eval after 24h
kj: also add a fallback policy mapping to balboa21b-fp16 for any host that triggers >3 evictions in 10m (auto-failover)
talia: will create canary and patch config in infra repo, add metric alerts for kernel_evictions, kv_evict_rate, and mem_frag_index. I'll also post the eval link once complete: https://internal-run/results/1765432199
sam: nice. if you need me to change default_max_new_tokens in model-catalog I can patch it — want 256 as the default for balboa21b-int4?
talia: yes set 256 for int4 canal variant, keep 512 for fp16 stable variant.
kj: one more thought: consider a quick compaction job during low-traffic window (auto-compact every 2h idle). helps long-lived fragmentation.
talia: good call. adding to runbook.
perf-bot: action items created: ART-573 (config patch), ART-574 (eval job), ART-575 (alert thresholds)
sam: thanks all. ping me if the canary hits odd regression.
talia: thanks — will update thread after first canary run (starting in ~15m). :rocket:
